elements.element: Early-termination fee is capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' Charges for the terminated Services"

elements.element: That capped early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer on termination
elements.evidence: "will be Customer's sole liability and IBM's sole and exclusive remedy in respect of such termination"

elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A" — a Customer-payable termination charge remains, merely capped
clause retains a Customer-payable charge on termination rather than eliminating it

offending_extra_words: and IBM's sole and exclusive remedy in respect of such termination
reasons: Fallback is met on its material terms: the early-termination charge is capped at three (3) months' Charges and is expressly Customer's sole liability for the termination, so the clause sits at the accepted fallback.
Preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) is not achieved — a capped charge is still payable — which is consistent with the drafter's locked fallback target.

Minimality fails: the insertion expands 18 words to 55 (ratio ~3.06) and changes ~65% of the characters, exceeding the official gates. A tighter proviso such as "; such charges will not exceed three (3) months' Charges and are Customer's sole liability for such termination" would suffice.

"IBM's sole and exclusive remedy" adds a remedy-exclusivity concept beyond the fallback's requirement of a sole liquidated amount payable by Customer — duplicative protection not needed to complete the level.
No unrelated commercial term is disturbed; the Attachment A / Service Option Attachment mechanic and defined terms (Charges, Services, Customer) remain effective, so intent is preserved.
